questions.q: Why does Mara open the meeting with a one-sentence headline instead of walking through every setting changed on every server?
options: Because Dale asked for a written report instead of a meeting
Because Dale needs to know Hartwell is measurably safer and specifically how, not a line-by-line account of sshd_config
Because listing every setting would take less time
Because the runbook already covers every setting in detail
questions.explain: Leading with the answer, as this whole capstone sequence teaches, means stating the result in a sentence before diving into supporting technical detail a non-technical manager can't evaluate anyway.

questions.q: Why does Mara demonstrate the Sentinel rule live using Lesson 6's test scenarios, instead of just describing it in a slide?
options: Because Sentinel requires a live demo before a rule can be saved
Because watching the rule fire on the real pattern and stay quiet on a normal typo is far more convincing than a claim, and it directly answers Dale's unspoken worry about false alarms
Because KQL can't be explained in words
Because the test scenarios are required for billing purposes
questions.explain: Seeing both the true positive and the correctly silent near-miss builds more trust than any description, because it answers the real question a manager has about a new detection rule.

questions.q: What is the "unspoken worry" this lesson says every manager has about a new detection rule?
options: Whether the rule will slow down the network
Whether the rule is going to bury their team in false alarms
Whether the rule requires a new software license
Whether the rule will work on weekends
questions.explain: A manager approving a new alert implicitly worries about alert fatigue — showing the rule stays silent on a normal typo directly addresses that concern.

questions.q: Why does Mara specifically mention that "everything is written down in a runbook" when presenting to Dale?
options: Because it's a formality required by Hartwell's HR department
Because it answers Lesson 1's underlying worry — Dale didn't want a one-time fix only Mara could maintain, he wanted something the team could rely on going forward
Because the runbook replaces the need for the Sentinel rule
Because Dale asked for a printed copy specifically
questions.explain: The runbook point ties the presentation back to the original ask from Lesson 1 — not finding out about problems after the fact, in a way that outlasts any one person.

questions.q: What are the three parts of the structure this lesson recommends for presenting the findings?
options: Introduction, methodology, conclusion
The headline, the how (at a level Dale can evaluate), and the proof, live
Risks, costs, benefits
Scope, baseline, detection target
questions.explain: Headline first, then the how at a non-technical level, then a live demonstration as proof — mirroring the "answer first, detail second" structure used elsewhere in this capstone sequence.
